column4: Wrap a cloth bandage around the wound to slow bleeding and protect from infection.
Tightly bind a limb to completely stop blood flow. Last resort for severe bleeding.
Use needle and thread to close a deep wound. Significantly improves healing.
Thoroughly clean a wound to prevent infection. Essential first step of treatment.
Immobilize a fractured bone with sticks and binding to allow proper healing.
Manipulate a dislocated joint back into its socket. Painful but necessary.
Apply cooling and protective dressing to burns. Prevents infection and speeds healing.
Gradually warm a hypothermic patient with blankets and body heat.
Rapidly cool an overheated patient with water and shade.
Give antibiotics to fight bacterial infections. Highly effective against sepsis.
Position patient properly, keep warm, and elevate legs to treat circulatory shock.
Give fluids to treat dehydration. Clean water or electrolyte solution.
Administer charcoal and fluids to absorb toxins and prevent dehydration.
Administer antiparasitic medicine to eliminate internal parasites.
Slowly warm frostbitten tissue. Do not rub. Apply protective dressings.
Give pain medication to reduce suffering and allow function despite injuries.
Cardiopulmonary resuscitation to restore heartbeat and breathing.
